task: Cycle 6 C6-01: wide Hadamard-rotated Muon W4A4 QAT and cross-block activation quantization mitigation (50m three-seed study, 120m real-checkpoint hardware NVFP4 transfer) on Blackwell

kernel_parity.reference: micro_rotated_ptq rotation (FP32) + nvfp4_encode + pack_e2m1 + to_blocked; every case also checks the embedded C4-02 quantizer

cross_mix_parity.reference: FP32 cross-block mix, then micro_rotated_ptq block-16 rotation + nvfp4_encode + pack_e2m1 + to_blocked

analysis.endpoints: nll: final NLL of the quantized (or BF16) model; delta_nll: quantized minus the BF16 NLL of the same checkpoint (0 for a BF16 side). Contrast differences are x - y; lower is better.

caveats: Statistics have df = 2 (3 paired seeds): the two-sided t-test has little power and the exact sign-flip p-value cannot fall below 0.25, so no sign-flip result can be significant. Holm-Bonferroni runs inside one part, split and endpoint; 'ties' means the difference is not significant, not that it is zero.
Part B arms share the token budget: 320 steps (10,485,760 tokens), the same batches, and cooldown arms branch from the Muon run at step 272.

Part C token budgets differ. The baseline has 640 steps (20,971,520 tokens); bf16_continue and qat_cooldown add 96 steps (3,145,728 tokens, +15.0%) on new train.bin batches at the terminal learning rate (x0.1). bf16_continue is the token-matched control for qat_cooldown; a contrast of qat_cooldown with the baseline mixes the QAT effect with the extra tokens.
Part C cooldowns start Muon momentum and the auxiliary AdamW from zero: the preserved C5-03 checkpoints hold weights only.

Selections use val.bin only: the wide QAT family (kron_hadamard_full), the best wide PTQ method (cross_full_butterfly_b16_gptq), the transfer arm (qat_wide_dual_cooldown), the best method of every arm, and the AWQ alpha of every (checkpoint, method). The 'best method' of an arm is chosen per arm, so a best-vs-best contrast compares deployment pipelines, not one method.
AWQ alphas are [0.0, 0.25, 0.5] (C5-03 used [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75]); alpha is chosen per checkpoint on val.bin with live hardware W4A4 dynamic scoring.

Wide rotations run a cross-block mix as FP32 PyTorch matrix products before the fused NVFP4 quantizer (only the block-16 part is in the kernel). Inference latency of that extra pass is not measured here, and the hardware rows are perplexity results, not speed results.

QAT fake quantization is FP32 round-to-nearest NVFP4 of both operands with a BF16 GEMM; training does not run the FP4 GEMM. Final rows requantize the weights with RTN or GPTQ and run the native FP4 GEMM.

Step times are wall clock per optimizer step on one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (sm_120) that also drives a desktop; the ratio to the plain run of the same seed over the same steps is the throughput result. Part B full-run arms compare all 320 steps, cooldown arms the last 48.
The dual loss weight (0.5 BF16 / 0.5 W4A4), the cooldown lengths and the arm list were fixed before the canonical run; QAT settings were developed on the synthetic shakedown only.
GPU training is seeded (initial state, batch stream) but not claimed to be bit-reproducible; the checkpoints are retained outside git with their tensor and file SHA-256 values.

test.bin is held out from every selection of this run (it is mapped once, after the freeze), but it is not an unseen holdout at study level: earlier cycles scored it, and C5-03 scored the same preserved 120m checkpoints with hadamard_b16_gptq and awq_w4a4_adaptive_butterfly_b16_gptq.
The C6-01 test-access log (artifacts/c6_01_run_evidence/test_access_log.jsonl) had 0 earlier openings of test.bin by this driver when this run mapped it.

The c5_03_baseline rows re-measure C5-03 methods on the same checkpoints in this session (max |NLL difference| to the published C5-03 rows: 0.00e+00 nats). The contrasts use the rows of this run, not the published values.
